fields.summary: Autonomous plan run, no owner. Research reproduced the leak on current code: running TestWritesThroughIndexMatchFold, TestAddKeysAndParent, TestCarveKeepsIDs and TestReviewCheckQuestionInNodeChangeSet with TMPDIR set to a scratch folder left 29 rhiza-projection-* folders in the real /tmp, each with an un-checkpointed index.db-wal (never closed). Cause: workspace.projection() in internal/api/projection.go, when a workspace was opened with openWorkspace and given no projection, opens one over a bare &Ctx{Root, Now, IDs}: no Getenv, so userdir.Temp gives /tmp, and no liveProjections, so guardProjections neither sees it open nor finds its folder in the test's TMPDIR. The test helper ctxWorkspace (change_test.go) and six direct openWorkspace calls in tests open such workspaces and never close them; 23 test files use ctxWorkspace. Every production caller of openWorkspace (status.go, run_model_cache.go readModel, openCtxWorkspace, openRootWorkspace) gives a projection first, so the fallback serves only tests. openWriteIndex already removes a throwaway folder on close and on a failed open. Snapshot builds and testCtxNoIndex use testCache as Getenv, which answers no TMPDIR, so their throwaway indexes also go to /tmp (closed, but outside any guard). The leak is from change set 01M7GFTKCA (one read path, #606), which served m39-one-read-path. On open-pr memory: its pre-push check runs rhiza check in-process over a fresh checkout (ship_prepush.go prePushRhizaCheck), and rhiza check alone on this repo (7,298 log entries) peaked at 832 MB RSS. The planner asked whether that memory work belongs here; the arbiter ruled (Decision open-pr-memory-separate) to keep this change set on the leak and put the memory work in its own discovered-from draft change set.
fields.title: Plan of the throwaway projections leak fix (autonomous)
